_readme: All assessment content lives here. Edit the wording freely. Keep each area's 'id' unchanged once assessments exist, because saved assessments refer to it. 'guidance' is the list of bullet prompts shown in the collapsible Guidance panel.

defaults._note: Starting values for Settings. Staff list is pre-filled; edit it in Settings. Set the next risk ref number to follow on from the last one in the Risk Register.

warnings.noCodes: Do not enter key-safe codes, door codes or passwords anywhere in this app. Do not write the codes down.
warnings.deviceSecurity: You are responsible for the security of this phone. Keep its own passcode switched on.
warnings.dpia: A Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) should be completed by Daisy Homecare before real client data is used in this app.

areas.title: Access to home
areas.question: Is there easy access and exit, with more than one exit, and are doors easily opened and unobstructed?
guidance: Key-safe security: do not write codes down; scramble the numbers on leaving
Safe access to dustbins

areas.title: Internal household
areas.question: Are surfaces level and uncluttered (wires, rugs, carpet joins), with adequate space to work?
guidance: Wash space, bath aids and chairs serviced and charged
Hygiene assistance level (OT instruction?)
Unfitted carpets or rugs and trip hazards: can edges be taped, can the client lift their foot over a rug?
Difficulty using equipment (OT referral?)
Clear working surfaces
Smoke alarms working
Link line (red alarm) present or needed
Electrical outlets safe and not overloaded
Water, gas and electricity working; service contracts in place if faults

areas.title: Steps / stairs
areas.question: Are steps and stairs non-slip, level and solid, and is any stair lift installed and in date?
guidance: Is the client safe on the stairs?
Let them reach the top first
Non-slip mats
Stair lift serviced

areas.title: Kitchen
areas.question: Are appliances and fire-safety equipment present and in date, and are electrics and gas safe?
guidance: Cooker in good order; gas not left on
Fire blanket or extinguisher present and PAT tested
Electrical appliances safe
Clean, hygienic, clear work area

areas.title: Lighting and neighbourhood
areas.question: Is the home and approach well lit, are dark places identified, and is the general area safe, with safe lit parking close to the home?
guidance: Porch, sensor and street lighting
Front garden structure, trees, obstructions
Carry a torch if needed
Parking details (driveway, zones, times)

areas.title: Pets
areas.question: Are pets adequately restrained? Discuss at the introductory visit.
guidance: Be sensitive: pets are family
Service pet?
Carer asthma or allergies
No risk of an animal escaping when entering or leaving

areas.title: Route from public transport to the home
areas.question: Is the route from public transport to the home safe, for carers and for the client on outings?
guidance: Travelling to and from work: bus stop location, distance, timetable (especially late at night)
Escorting the client on outings: can they walk to the stop, are they safe on a bus, wheelchair or mobility aid on the bus

areas.title: Other people living in the home
areas.question: Do other people in the home or nearby present any risk?
guidance: Spouse, children, family, friends, shared-home scenarios
Others in a complex and close neighbours

areas.title: History of aggressive behaviour or potential violence
areas.question: Is there any history of aggressive behaviour or potential violence, by the client or close associates?
guidance: Criminal history
Patterns of disruptive behaviour or abuse
Drug or alcohol problems
Dementia or neurological conditions linked to aggression
Include neighbours

areas.title: Client a risk to themselves / other hazards
areas.question: Is the client a risk to themselves, for example through mental health issues or substance or alcohol misuse?
guidance: History of mental health issues leading to loss of control or self-harm
Registered with a mental health nurse
Behavioural signs, broken furniture or windows

areas.title: Storage of medicines and substances
areas.question: Are medicines and other substances stored safely?
guidance: Dangerous medicines
Out of reach or locked away
Capable of safe self-medication
Packed in a measurable way (e.g. dosette box)

areas.title: Medication requirements
areas.question: Are the client's medication requirements clear, and can they be met safely?
guidance: Odd instructions explained and noted on the medication record
Does the care plan say when and how to give?
Self-medication ability
Alternative ingestion (crushing, PEG)
Complex drugs (warfarin, morphine, antibiotics) charted differently

areas.title: PPE requirements
areas.question: What personal protective equipment (PPE) is needed, and who supplies it?
guidance: Bodily-fluid contact
Communicable disease (e.g. HIV, MRSA, shingles)
Compromised immune system (e.g. chemotherapy)
Foot covers, aprons, gloves (latex-free?), masks, eyewear
Supplied at home or by the carer

areas.title: Allergies and intolerances
areas.question: Does the client have any allergies or intolerances, and are they listed on the care plan?
guidance: Known allergies and reactions
Do you know how to use an EpiPen?
Intolerances and aversions
Common allergens (shellfish, nuts, penicillin, foods, soaps and fragrances, latex)
Listed on the care plan

areas.title: Other safety issues with premises or person
areas.question: Is there anything else about the premises or the person that gives a sense of unease?
guidance: Block of flats, stairs or lifts
Do you feel safe and have good rapport?

areas.title: Other agencies supporting the client
areas.question: Which other agencies support the client, and can a care team be formed around them?
guidance: Names and contact details so a care team can form
District nurse, social care, community care agency, volunteer groups, mental health nurse, Link Line, Parkinson's nurse, etc.
